items.excerpt: Everyone is spending a fortune making AI smarter, but the missing layer is hospitality — the service design craft of anticipating need and handing off gracefully. The piece argues designers, not model labs, own that gap.

A working model for AI-enabled UX research in which the researcher governs rather than delegates: which parts of synthesis, recruiting and analysis AI can run, and where human judgment must stay in the loop.

The 1982 film and its sequel predicted the design problems teams are still failing to solve — synthetic memory, trust, and the interfaces designers argue about daily. A craft read on AI interface design.
Real restaurant menus generated with AI image tools are replacing vernacular "folk" graphic design with uncanny slop. A concrete look at what happens to everyday brand craft when generation is free.
The Hamnet poster row shows AI accusations now land on human-made work by default — a new provenance burden that designers and studios have to design around.
Apple's new Mac mini claymation spot was made by hand, and Apple released a behind-the-scenes film to prove it — human craft is becoming an explicit brand signal in the AI era.

Meta's Muse Image model is now callable through Vercel AI Gateway with one API key, automatic fallbacks and spend tracking — lowering the setup cost of wiring image generation into product and design tooling.
AI Gateway can now run video generation as a background job with webhooks, start/status pairs or polling — making long-running generative video practical inside real product workflows.
A walkthrough of five new UI/UX features in Claude Code, led by the /design command that lets the terminal agent draw and iterate on UI directly — shifting where frontend design work starts.

Marver is a free, open-source alternative to paper.design and pen.dev: a shared canvas computed from your local files so you can align with an AI agent visually — spec, wireframe and design in working code.
Why image models still mangle typography inside generated images, and the prompting and compositing workarounds that actually hold up for posters, packaging and ad layouts.

Meriem Benhabiles brings structured UX thinking to dashboards — the questions to ask before opening a tool, and the decisions that determine whether an insight actually lands. Directly relevant as AI floods teams with generated charts.
Theia, Spare Parts 3D's tool that turns 2D drawings into 3D CAD models, avoids AI garbage output with an age-old trick: a human verification step built into the generation loop.
CG Channel's weekly roundup of the DCC, render and AI-assisted tool releases that slipped past — a fast scan of what changed in the 3D and visualisation pipeline.

Smart Remesh is a context-aware Blender add-on that turns both organic characters and hard-surface models into clean quad geometry while preserving vertex positions — automating one of 3D's most tedious steps.
Google says Gemini 3.5 Transcribe turns rambling speech into structured text and will soon work in any web field in Chrome — a quiet input-method shift for research notes, briefs and design docs.

Meta introduced Meta XR Operator, an experimental tool that lets AI coding agents autonomously build, test, debug and visually verify VR apps — closing the build-test-verify loop for spatial design teams.
Google is testing a 'Listening area' mode for Live Translate on Android XR — a headline interaction pattern for its upcoming smart glasses and a concrete example of spatial AI UI design.

Salesforce and Anthropic launched Claudeforce, putting the whole CRM inside Claude via a CoWork plugin with 37 prebuilt skills — enterprises reaching data through an AI interface instead of a designed UI.

With agents deployed across every channel, the hard problem has moved from automation to orchestration — shared context layers so AI systems, apps and humans hand off cleanly instead of siloing the customer experience.
Microsoft Design profiles a company that now runs more AI agents than employees — what that does to org design, handoffs and the shape of creative teams.
A quick demo of an AI system generating explorable 3D worlds from a prompt — the kind of world-model capability that is starting to matter for environment and spatial designers.
Figma's motion team walks through path trim, one of the new Figma Motion primitives — the craft layer designers still own as generated UI takes over static layout.
